Buddy, also grew up a runner}} ({{IPAc-en|h|iː|l|d}} {{respell|HEELD}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 17, 2024}} born December 17, 1992){{cite web|first=James|last=Ham|title=Buddy Hield is 26, not 25, as Kings guard reveals age incorrectly listed|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/buddy-hield-26-not-25-kings-guard-reveals-age-incorrectly-listed?amp|website=NBCSports.com|date=December 20, 2018|access-date=December 21, 2018}} is a Bahamian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]] and was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] in 2015 and 2016.{{cite web|title=Buddy Hield Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Buddy-Hield/Summary/42415|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 12, 2015}}{{cite web|title=Buddy Hield Biography|url=http://www.soonersports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=208409509|website=SoonerSports.com|access-date=March 12, 2015}} In 2016, Hield received four major national player of the year awards: the [[John R. Wooden Award]], the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Award]], [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''Sporting News'' Player of the Year]], and the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]]. He was selected with the sixth overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] and was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for [[DeMarcus Cousins]] in 2017. Hield was dealt to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in a package for [[Domantas Sabonis]] in 2022. In February 2024, he was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. In July 2024, Hield was involved in a six-team trade that involved him getting traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. In February 2026, he was traded to the Atlanta Hawks. ==Early life== Hield grew up in [[Eight Mile Rock]], a coastal region west of [[Freeport, The Bahamas|Freeport]], in the [[West Grand Bahama]] district in [[the Bahamas]].Hield, Buddy. [http://www.theplayerstribune.com/buddy-hield-oklahoma-sooners-basketball/], The Players Tribune, March 17, 2016. He was fifth of seven children of his mother Jackie Braynen.{{cite news |last=Tracy |first=Marc |date=March 14, 2016 |title=For Buddy Hield and Other Bahamians, Talent Is Cultivated on the Great Plains |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/03/14/sports/ncaabasketball/sunrise-christian-academy-bahamas-buddy-hield.html?_r=0 |newspaper=New York Times |location=[[New York City|New York]] |access-date=April 12, 2016}} Hield received his nickname from his mother after [[Bud Bundy]] of the sitcom ''[[Married... with Children]]''.{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Vecenie |title=Oklahoma's Buddy Hield fueled by his roots of growing up in Bahamas |date=August 13, 2015 |work=CBS Sports |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25267076/oklahomas-buddy-hield-fueled-by-his-bahamian-roots }} Hield attended Jack Hayward High School in Freeport.{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Aaron |title=Buddy Hield's Home Court |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/buddy-hields-home-court/ |website=Vice |access-date=March 18, 2024 |date=March 18, 2016}} He was first featured in high school by ''The All Bahamian Brand'', a basketball magazine from the Bahamas. Hield, as a young eighth-grader, was rated by the All-Bahamian Brand as the best eighth grader in the Bahamas and one to watch. Hield showed his early ability to lead his team from a young age by taking his Jack Hayward basketball team to the championship of the Providence Holiday Tournament on a buzzer-beater and also leading his team to win the Grand Bahamas High School Championships. For his exploits, Hield was named an All Bahamian Brand All Bahamian Selection.{{Citation|title = SportsMEDIAoNe2009-2010allBahamianTeamVideo.mov|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Dcq00aRWxM|date = August 26, 2010|access-date = February 6, 2016|last = SportsMEDIAoNe1}} After his performances in The Bahamas, Hield was recruited to attend [[Sunrise Christian Academy]] in [[Bel Aire, Kansas|Bel Aire]], a basketball prep school in a suburb of [[Wichita, Kansas]]. Former [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] assistant and then-Sunrise coach Kyle Lindsted recruited the 6-foot 4-inch (1.93 m) guard. In 2011, during Hield's junior year at Sunrise Christian, he led the team to the National Association of Christian Athletes national championship, getting named the MVP of the tournament.{{cite news |last=King |first=Jason |date=November 19, 2015 |title=Bahamas' Best: Buddy Hield's Relentless Journey to Oklahoma and Hoops Stardom |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2590353-bahamas-best-buddy-hields-relentless-journey-to-oklahoma-and-hoops-stardom |newspaper=[[Bleacher Report]] |location=[[San Francisco]] |access-date=April 6, 2016 |quote=As the 86th-ranked player in the 2012 class by Rivals.com, Hield had been offered a scholarship by tradition-rich Kansas prior to his senior season. But he canceled his official visit and committed to Oklahoma following a trip to Norman, where Kruger had been hired to resurrect a dormant program.}} As a senior in the 2011–12 season, Hield averaged 22.7 points on .491 shooting in 21.0 minutes per game. Hield was highly recruited and selected the [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma Sooners]] over the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]].{{cite news |last=Robinett |first=Kellis |date=February 4, 2016 |title=High school stop in Wichita gave OU's Buddy Hield a path to success |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/article58483728.html#storylink=cpy |newspaper=[[Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=April 8, 2016 }}{{cite news |last=Young |first=RJ |date=January 18, 2013 |title=OU's Buddy Hield won't back down from challenge |url=https://oklahoma.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=1461800 |newspaper=[[Rivals.com]] |location=[[Sunnyvale, California]] |access-date=April 7, 2016 |quote=Of those three, Kansas seems the obvious choice for a basketball player -- especially one who played high school ball in the Sunflower State. Jayhawk basketball is as rich in tradition and committed to winning championships as any program in the country. So why turn down Kansas men's basketball coach Bill Self if he offers you a scholarship?}}{{cite news|last1=Rexrode|first1=Joe|title=MSU's Nairn, OU's Hield represent Bahamas, friendship|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2015/03/25/michigan-state-spartans-oklahoma-tum-tum-nairn-buddy-hield/70469788/|access-date=June 24, 2015|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=March 25, 2015}}Dodd, Rustin. [http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article52858315.html As No. 1 vs. No. 2 showdown looms, Kansas guards prepare for matchup with Oklahoma’s Buddy Hield], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', January 3, 2016. "A native of the Bahamas, Hield, a 6-foot-4 shooting guard, had gone to Sunrise to pursue a college basketball scholarship, and after two seasons in Kansas, he was a top-100 recruit with offers from schools all over the country. One of those schools was KU. The Jayhawks’ staff was interested in Hield, Self says." ==College career== [[File:Buddy Hield crop.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.85|Hield in January 2016]] As a freshman at Oklahoma, Hield scored 7.8 points per game and was the recipient of the team's Most Inspirational Award. He was a second-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] selection as a sophomore after averaging 16.5 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.4 steals per game. Hield worked on his defense prior to his junior year and expanded his offensive game to more of a high-volume [[Three-point field goal|three-point shooter]].{{cite news|last1=Olson|first1=Eric|title=Oklahoma's Buddy Hield thrives in the clutch|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/2015/03/25/oklahomas-buddy-hield-thrives-clutch/70466904/|access-date=June 24, 2015|work=[[The Detroit News]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 25, 2015}} Hield averaged 17.4 points and 5.4 rebounds per game as a junior at Oklahoma and shot 41 percent from the field. He led Oklahoma to a 24–11 record and Sweet 16 berth. Despite being a potential [[2015 NBA draft]] selection, Hield decided to return for his senior season.{{cite news|title=Big 12 Player of Year Hield returning to Oklahoma for senior season|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-returning-senior-season-no-nba-042415|access-date=April 25, 2015|work=[[Fox Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=April 24, 2015}} He was a first-team All-Big 12 selection and was named [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Sooners' Hield Leads All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209934691|website=[[Big 12 Conference]]|access-date=May 17, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}} Hield was listed on the [[Oscar Robertson Award]] preseason watchlist{{cite web|title=USBWA Unveils Award Watchlists|url=https://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2016/watchlists151202.html|website=[[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]]|access-date=December 22, 2015}} as well as the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] preseason watchlist.{{cite web|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2015/12/02/naismith-trophy-early-season-watch-list-released/|title=Naismith Trophy early season watch list released|access-date=December 3, 2015|date=December 2, 2015|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|author=Johnson, Raphielle}} He recorded a career-high of 46 points in a triple overtime loss to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] on January 4, 2016, receiving a standing ovation from the opposing crowd after a postgame interview with [[Scott Van Pelt]]. Hield's 46 points tied the record for most points scored by an opponent at [[Allen Fieldhouse]].{{cite news|last1=Mattioli|first1=Kami|title=Kansas fans stick around to show love for Oklahoma's Buddy Hield|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball-news/4690175-kansas-fans-stick-around-to-show-love-for-oklahomas-buddy-hield|access-date=January 6, 2016|work=[[The Sporting News]]|date=January 5, 2016}} He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the Naismith Trophy on February 11.{{cite news|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}} Following his senior year at Oklahoma, Hield won the [[John R. Wooden Award]] on April 7, 2016, as the best college basketball player for the 2015–16 season, averaging 25 points, 5.7 rebounds, two assists per game, and led the nation in three-point shots.{{cite news |last=O'Donnell |first=Ricky |date=April 8, 2016 |title=Oklahoma's Buddy Hield named 2016 Wooden Award winner |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2016/4/8/11396004/buddy-hield-named-2016-wooden-award-winner-oklahoma |newspaper=[[SB Nation]] |location=[[New York City]] |access-date=April 13, 2016}} {{clear left}} ==Professional career== ===New Orleans Pelicans (2016–2017)=== ====2016–17 season: All–Rookie Honors & mid–season trade==== On June 23, 2016, Hield was selected by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] with the sixth overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last=Reid|first=John|url=http://www.nola.com/pelicans/index.ssf/2016/06/new_orleans_pelicans_select_in.html|title=New Orleans Pelicans select Buddy Hield with 6th overall pick in 2016 NBA Draft|work=NOLA.com|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=June 23, 2016}} On July 22, he signed with the Pelicans.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-2016-first-round-draft-pick-buddy-hield|title=Pelicans Sign 2016 First Round Draft Pick Buddy Hield|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2016|access-date=July 22, 2016}} On December 15, Hield had his best outing as a Pelican with 21 points and five three-pointers in a 102–95 victory over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899827|title=Davis, Hield lift Pelicans past Pacers, 102-95|work=ESPN.com|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}} On January 3, 2017, Hield was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for December.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/01/03/joel-embiid-buddy-hield-kia-rookies-month-december|title=Joel Embiid, Buddy Hield named Kia Rookies of the Month|work=NBA.com|date=January 3, 2017|access-date=January 4, 2017}} ===Sacramento Kings (2017–2022)=== On February 20, 2017, Hield was traded, along with [[Tyreke Evans]], [[Langston Galloway]] and 2017 first-round and second-round draft picks, to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for [[DeMarcus Cousins]] and [[Omri Casspi]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-hield-evans-galloway|title=Kings Acquire Hield, Evans, Galloway, and 2017 Draft Selections|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2017|access-date=February 20, 2017}} Hield made his Kings debut three days later, scoring 16 points off the bench in a 116–100 victory over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900261|title=Cauley-Stein scores 29, Kings beat Nuggets 116-100|work=ESPN.com|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}} He was named Western Conference Rookie of the Month for March.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2017/04/03/dario-saric-buddy-hield-kia-nba-rookies-month|title=Dario Saric, Buddy Hield named Kia NBA Rookies of the Month|work=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2017|access-date=April 4, 2017}} On April 11, Hield set a new career high with 30 points in a 129–104 victory over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900594|title=Hield, Lawson lead Kings past Suns, 129-104|work=ESPN.com|date=April 11, 2017|access-date=April 12, 2017}} At the end of the season, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie First Team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/release-062617|title=Buddy Hield Named to 2016-17 NBA All-Rookie First Team|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2017|access-date=June 27, 2017}} ====2017–18 season: Career-high three–point percentage==== Hield began the 2017–18 season as a starter before switching to a bench role and becoming the team's sixth man after seven games.{{cite web|last=Avila|first=Nick|url=https://www.hoop-ball.com/articles/team/player-review-buddy-hield-became-one-with-his-bench-role/|title=Player Review: Buddy Hield became one with his bench role|work=hoop-ball.com|date=April 27, 2018|access-date=November 2, 2018}} On November 25, 2017, Hield scored a season-high 27 points off the bench with a career-high seven three-pointers in a narrow 97–95 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|last=Jones|first=Jason|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/kings-blog/article186571498.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171209154410/http://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/kings-blog/article186571498.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2017|title=Kings get hard lesson in 'fool's gold' offense. Then Hield's career night falls short|work=sacbee.com|date=November 25, 2017|access-date=December 8, 2017}} He shot 43.1 percent from three-point range in 2017–18, which placed him ninth in the NBA among qualified players.{{cite web|last=Jeter|first=Christopher|url=https://hoopshabit.com/2018/06/11/sacramento-kings-2017-18-player-grades-buddy-hield/|title=Sacramento Kings: 2017-18 player grades for Buddy Hield|work=hoopshabit.com|date=June 11, 2018|access-date=November 2, 2018}} ====2018–19 season: Career-high points per game==== In December 2018, Hield had a seven-game streak with 20 points or more.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071187|title=Bench helps Clippers hang on for 127-118 win over Kings|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2018|access-date=December 27, 2018|quote=Buddy Hield scored 11, ending his seven-game streak with 20 or more.}} On January 5, 2019, he scored 32 points and had a career-high eight three-pointers in a 127–123 loss to the Warriors.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071259|title=Curry scores 42 points, Warriors hold off Kings 127-123|work=ESPN.com|date=January 5, 2019|access-date=January 6, 2019}} On January 19, Hield made an off-balance, fadeaway three-pointer just before time expired and scored 35 points in a narrow 103–101 victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071356|title=Hield beats buzzer, lifts Kings to 103-101 win over Pistons|work=ESPN.com|date=January 19, 2019|access-date=January 19, 2019}} On March 23, he had 25 points and broke the franchise season record for three-pointers in a 112–103 victory over the Suns. Hield made 7 of 14 shots from beyond the arc, giving him 245 three-pointers for the season and surpassing the mark of 240 set by [[Peja Stojaković]] in [[2003–04 Sacramento Kings season|2003–04]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071767|title=Hield sets franchise season record for 3s, Kings beat Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=March 23, 2019|access-date=March 24, 2019}} In April, he broke [[Damian Lillard]]'s NBA record (599) for most three-pointers made in a player's first three seasons.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071851|title=Kings bounce back from 25-point loss to beat Cavs 117-104|work=ESPN.com|date=April 4, 2019|access-date=April 11, 2019}}{{cite web|last=Ham|first=James|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/kings/buddy-hield-breaks-damian-lillards-nba-3-point-record-kings-finale|title=Buddy Hield breaks Damian Lillard's NBA 3-point record in Kings' finale|work=nbcsports.com|date=April 10, 2019|access-date=April 11, 2019}} ====2019–20 season: Contract extension==== On October 21, 2019, Hield signed a four-year, $94 million contract extension.{{cite web |title=Kings Sign Buddy Hield to Contract Extension |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/blog/kings-sign-buddy-hield-contract-extension |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=October 21, 2019}}{{cite web |title=Buddy Hield, Kings agree to 4-year extension |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-hield-kings-agree-extension |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=October 21, 2019}} On December 26, he accused coaches and teammates of having "trust issues" after he was benched late in regulation of a game that the Kings eventually lost in double overtime to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. Hield apologized to the whole team the next day for his remarks.{{cite web |title=Buddy Hield bemoans 'trust issues' after Kings' 2OT loss to Timberwolves |url=https://www.nba.com/news/hield-kings-trust-issues-coaches |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=December 27, 2019}} Hield eventually lost his starting spot to [[Bogdan Bogdanović (basketball)|Bogdan Bogdanović]], but the switch produced a boost in his production and efficiency; in only his second game off the bench, on January 27, 2020, and again against the Timberwolves, Hield scored a career-high 42 points to lead the Kings to a 133–129 overtime victory. Afterwards, Hield dedicated the game to his idol [[Kobe Bryant]], who died in a [[2020 Calabasas helicopter crash|helicopter accident]] the day prior.{{cite web |last1=Anderson |first1=Jason |title='Do it for Kobe': Buddy Hield scores 42 as Kings rally to beat Timberwolves in OT |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/article239702088.html |website=The Sacramento Bee |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=January 27, 2020}} On February 15, Hield won the [[Three-Point Contest]] at [[NBA All-Star Weekend]] in Chicago, topping [[Devin Booker]] 27–26 in the final round.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2876535-buddy-hield-wins-2020-nba-3-point-contest-scores-highlights-and-reaction|title=Buddy Hield Wins 2020 NBA 3-Point Contest: Scores, Highlights and Reaction|website=Bleacher Report|last=Zucker|first=Joseph|access-date=December 23, 2020|date=February 16, 2020}} ====2020–21 season: Fastest in NBA history to hit 1,000 3–pointers==== On December 23, 2020, Hield recorded 22 points, four rebounds, and three assists, alongside a game-winning, buzzer-beating tip-in, in a 124–122 overtime win against the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/kings-video-buddy-hield-insane-buzzer-beater-tip-in-sinks-nuggets-in-ot/|title=VIDEO: Buddy Hield's insane buzzer-beater tip-in sinks Nuggets in OT|website=ClutchPoints|last=Salao|first=Renzo|access-date=December 23, 2020|date=December 23, 2020}} On February 28, 2021, Hield became the fastest player in history to make 1,000 three-pointers, needing 350 games only to reach the mark, but that record has since been broken by [[Duncan Robinson]].{{cite web |title=Monk's three-point play helps Hornets stun Kings 127-126 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401267688 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=February 28, 2021}}{{cite web |title=Buddy Hield fastest in NBA history to make 1,000 career 3-pointers |url=https://www.nba.com/news/buddy-hield-fastest-in-nba-history-to-make-1000-career-3-pointers |website=NBA.com |access-date=March 1, 2021 |date=March 1, 2021}} On July 29, 2021, it was reported that the Kings were moving towards a deal sending Hield to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for forwards [[Kyle Kuzma]] and [[Montrezl Harrell]].{{cite web |title=Buddy Hield traded to Lakers |url=https://twitter.com/wojespn/status/1420852216601186305 |website=twitter.com |access-date=July 29, 2021 |date=July 29, 2021}} The deal fell through as the Lakers ended up trading Kuzma and Harrell in a package to the [[Washington Wizards]] for [[Russell Westbrook]].{{cite web |title=Lakers Acquire Russell Westbrook |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-acquire-russell-westbrook-2021 |website=NBA.com |access-date=August 6, 2021 |date=August 6, 2021}} ===Indiana Pacers (2022–2024)=== ====2021–22 season: Mid–season trade==== On February 8, 2022, Hield, [[Tyrese Haliburton]], and [[Tristan Thompson]] were traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Justin Holiday]], [[Jeremy Lamb]], [[Domantas Sabonis]], and a 2023 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-tyrese-haliburton-buddy-hield-and-tristan-thompson-kings|title=Pacers Acquire Tyrese Haliburton, Buddy Hield, and Tristan Thompson from Kings|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2022}} Three days later, Hield made his Pacers debut, starting alongside Haliburton in a 120–113 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], recording a near triple double with 16 points, eight assists, and nine rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2022/02/11/pacers-vs-cavs-tyrese-haliburton-shines-but-caris-levert-gets-win/6688664001/|title=Tyrese Haliburton shines in Pacers debut, but Caris LeVert leads Cavs to win in his return|last=Boyd|first=James|website=indystar.com|date=February 11, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2022}} On February 15, Hield scored a season-high 36 points on 8–12 three-point shooting, while dishing out four assists in a 128–119 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-buddy-hield-goes-off-for-season-high-36-points/|title=Pacers' Buddy Hield: Goes off for season-high 36 points|website=CBS Sports|date=February 15, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2022}} ====2022–23 season: Franchise record for most threes made in a season==== On December 5, Hield became the second-fastest player in NBA history to reach 1,500 career three-pointers, only behind [[Stephen Curry]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/videos/hield-hits-three-no-1500|title=Hield Hits Three No. 1500|website=NBA.com|date=December 5, 2022|access-date=December 6, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/hield-shooting-his-way-into-the-record-books|title=Hield Shooting His Way Into the Record Books|website=NBA.com|date=December 28, 2022|access-date=March 2, 2023|author=Hotchkiss, Wheat}}{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/Pacers/status/1599994381032771584|title=@Pacers status update|date=December 5, 2022|accessdate=March 2, 2023|publisher=[[Twitter]]}} On December 27, Hield tied a then season-high 28 points on 6-of-7 three-point shooting, along with nine rebounds in a 129–114 victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ballysports.com/indiana/news/hield-haliburton-carry-pacers-to-129-114-victory-over-hawks|title=Hield, Haliburton carry Pacers to 129-114 victory over Hawks|website=BallySports.com|date=December 27, 2022|access-date=December 28, 2022}} Two days later, with a three-pointer against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] just three seconds into the game, Hield scored the fastest field goal recorded in NBA history since the [[1996–97 NBA season]], passing [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Fame]] Pacer [[Reggie Miller]].{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/extrastatmuse/status/1608629295068635136|title=Buddy Hield recorded the quickest 3PM in a game since tracking began in 1997.|website=StatMuse.com|date=December 29, 2022|access-date=December 29, 2022}} On January 11, 2023, Hield posted a new season-high 31 points, eight rebounds, and 7-of-15 three-point shooting in a loss to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/videos/buddy-hield-31-points-8-rebounds-indiana-pacers-at-new-york-knicks|title=Buddy Hield 31 Points & 8 Rebounds |website=NBA.com|date=January 11, 2023|access-date=January 11, 2023}} On February 15, he put up 27 points in a 117–113 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Hield also made his 230th three-pointer of the season, surpassing [[Reggie Miller]] for the most three-pointers made in a season in Pacers history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/pacers-news-buddy-hield-demolishes-reggie-miller-3pt-record-in-21-less-games|title=Pacers sharpshooter Buddy Hield demolishes Reggie Miller 3PT record in 21 less games|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=February 15, 2023|access-date=February 15, 2023}} Hield and [[2023 NBA All-Star Game|All–Star]] teammate [[Tyrese Haliburton]] were selected to participate in the [[NBA Three-Point Contest|2023 NBA Three-Point Contest]], where they both lost in the finals to [[Damian Lillard]].{{Cite web |title=2023 Starry 3-Point Contest|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-3-point-contest |access-date=2023-02-17 |website=NBA.com}} ==== 2023–24 season: Assisting Pacers' ascension ==== Before the start of the [[2023–24 Indiana Pacers season|2023–24 season]], Hield changed his jersey number for the first time in his career, switching from 24 to 7, formerly worn by Pacers [[Jermaine O'Neal]], [[Al Jefferson]], [[Malcolm Brogdon]], and [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]].{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers guard Buddy Hield changing jersey number from 24 to 7 |url=https://www.si.com/nba/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-guard-buddy-hield-changing-jersey-number-from-24-to-7#:~:text=The%20Indiana%20Pacers%20announced%20on,switching%20from%2024%20to%207. |access-date=2023-09-14 |website=SI.com |language=en}} In back-to-back games coming off the bench, Hield scored 19 points, once in a one-point loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on November 4, and again in a 41-point victory against rookie [[Victor Wembanyama]] and the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on November 6, giving head coach [[Rick Carlisle]] his 900th career win.{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/haliburton-pacers-carlisle-900th-win-152-111-rout-104677194|title=THaliburton, Pacers get Carlisle his 900th win with 152-111 rout of Buddy Hield: Scores easy 19 points|website=CBSSports.com|last=Staff|first=RotoWire|date=November 7, 2023|access-date=November 7, 2023}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2024)=== On February 8, 2024, Hield was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a three-team deal involving the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Buddy Hield Acquired by 76ers in Three-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/buddy-hield-acquired-at-trade-deadline|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} The next day, he made his 76ers debut, putting up 20 points and six assists in a 127–121 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|first=Sam|last=DiGiovanni|title=Buddy Hield, Cam Payne react to first game with 76ers|url=https://clutchpoints.com/76ers-news-buddy-hield-cam-payne-react-to-first-game-with-philly|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=February 9, 2024|access-date=February 9, 2024}} Hield played in a league-high total of 84 games in the [[2023-24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], averaging 12.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers' Buddy Hield logs 86 games before playoffs|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39965430/philadelphia-76ers-buddy-hield-logs-86-games-playoffs|access-date=April 26, 2024|website=[[ESPN]]|language=en}} ===Golden State Warriors (2024–2026)=== On July 6, 2024, Hield signed a four-year, $37.8 million contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]] via a six-team sign-and-trade also including the Minnesota Timberwolves, Dallas Mavericks, Denver Nuggets, and Charlotte Hornets, which became the NBA's first six-team transaction.{{cite web|title=Warriors Acquire Kyle Anderson & Buddy Hield in Six-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-kyle-anderson-amp-buddy-hield-in-six-team-trade-20240706|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}} Hield made his Warriors debut on October 23, putting up 22 points with five three-pointers made and five rebounds in 15 minutes played off the bench in a 139–104 victory over the [[2024–25 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-buddy-hield-shares-eye-opening-take-about-new-teammates-egos|title= Warriors' Buddy Hield shares eye-opening take about new teammates' egos|website=ClutchPoints|last=Bologna|first=Ryan|date=October 23, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}} Two days later, Hield put up 27 points with seven three-pointers made in a 127–86 victory over the [[2024–25 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]]. He put up a total of 12 three-pointers made across his first two career games with the Warriors, the most three-pointers made by a player in his first two games with a team in NBA history.{{cite web|url= https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-buddy-hield-makes-nba-history-early-6moy-year-case-in-blowout-win-over-jazz|title= Warriors' Buddy Hield makes NBA history, early 6MOY Year case in win over Jazz next game he went 0 for 50 in a career bad game|website=ClutchPoints|last=Winter|first=Jack|date=October 25, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}} Hield played in all 82 games for Golden State during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], posting averages of 11.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 1.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=11 NBA iron men who played all 82 games this season, including an old and tiny Chris Paul|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2025/4/14/24408190/nba-players-all-82-games-appear-ironman-chris-paul-mikal-bridges|access-date=July 19, 2025|website=sbnation.com|language=en}} On May 4, 2025, Hield put up 33 points on nine three-pointers made in a 103–89 Game 7 win over the [[2024–25 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]] to eliminate them in the first round. His nine three-pointers tied [[Donte DiVincenzo]]'s record for the most made three-pointers in a playoff game 7.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/warriors-news-buddy-hield-ties-bonkers-game-7-record-to-shoot-dubs-past-rockets|title=Buddy Hield ties bonkers Game 7 record to shoot Warriors past Rockets|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pagaduan|first=Jedd|date=May 4, 2025|access-date=May 4, 2025}} His six three-pointers made in the first half, were an NBA playoff game 7 first half record and tied the record for any half of a game 7 (also with DiVincenzo).{{cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/buddy-hield-shuts-up-hater-warriors-fans-record-20309805.php|title=Buddy Hield shuts up hater Warriors fans with record-breaking Game 7|accessdate=May 6, 2025|date=May 4, 2025|publisher=[[SFGate]]|author=Fernandez, Gabe}} Hield made 44 appearances (including three starts) for Golden State during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 8.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Buddy Hield 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2990984/buddy-hield|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2026–present)=== On February 5, 2026, Hield and [[Jonathan Kuminga]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Kristaps
